brief: BTIG's technical note argues equity indices are consolidating before a downside break. QQQ has traded inside its 8/4 range for 27 trading days, and Bollinger Bands are the tightest since March, so BTIG expects a lower resolution. Nearly 5% of the Russell 3000 hit 52-week lows while the index itself sits under 3% from a 52-week high, a breadth divergence that is historically a coin flip over 20 days but has preceded major drops in 2000, 2007, 2015, 2018, 2020, 2021 and 2026. Semis (SOXX) remain below a declining 50-day average, with a 200-day test (-17%) seen as likely. IWM has spent ten days below its 50-day average and could test its 200-day level this month, though the long-term uptrend still holds. Separately, 10-year real rates just hit a cycle high after three years of consolidation, and despite negative bond sentiment BTIG will not call a major top. AUD/JPY, which tracks SPX, has pulled back toward the lower end of its range, a possible equity headwind. Tanker shipping costs (BWET) are up nearly 500% since June and likely to unwind. OIH fell despite WTI crude above $100, which BTIG reads as energy weakness, not bullish, raising correlation-one risk.
